stem.en: Kabir says "a gene for brown eyes is a picture of a brown eye, written in DNA". What does a gene actually contain?

text.en: The order of amino acids for one protein, or one RNA tool. Brown eyes come from several proteins that make and place a pigment, each from its own gene. No gene draws an eye. A recipe, not a drawing.

feedback.en: DNA has four letters and no drawings. The tape spells bead orders. The eye is what thousands of proteins do together.
There is no colour in a gene. There is a recipe for a protein that, in a cell, helps make a pigment.

text.en: A list of every cell in the eye.

feedback.en: No gene knows about cells. Genes spell proteins. Cells are what proteins, and Book VII, build.

explanation.en: A gene spells one chain. The route from chain to trait runs through folding, enzymes, cells and signals, all of Books IV to VII. Most traits use many genes.
